meta.title: BESCOM exception scenarios — citizen-evidence pass
meta.disclaimer: Research handoff, not official advice or an application route. Redacted public first-person reports identify case-specific friction only; they do not establish BESCOM eligibility, tenant authority, consent or OTP requirements, arrears liability, deceased-consumer procedure, or a remedy.

scenarios.label: Tenant
scenarios.summary: A tenant faces a BESCOM account issue while the property owner is unavailable or uncooperative.

scenarios.label: Previous consumer deceased
scenarios.summary: A successor seeks a name transfer where the recorded consumer has died.

scenarios.label: Consent unavailable
scenarios.summary: A prospective transferee cannot use the previous consumer's or builder's recorded contact route.

sources.title: BESCOM connection transfer is now 100% online and faceless
sources.notes: Public thread containing individual first-person comments about a name-transfer interface. Usernames, property/account identifiers, builder and previous-consumer identity, telephone details, payment amounts, and addresses are omitted. Comments and the original post are not treated as provider policy.

sources.title: Stuck in Electricity Billing Issue Between Flat Owner and BESCOM, Seeking Advice.
sources.notes: Public first-person tenant account. Exact bill amount, dates, location, meter history, tenant duration, owner/caretaker details, messages, and other identifying facts are omitted. It concerns billing and owner cooperation, not a reported completed or refused name-transfer application.

claims.text: One tenant reported that an electricity bill included charges attributed to a period before their tenancy and that the property owner was uncooperative, leaving the tenant concerned about the account's unpaid balance.
claims.notes: One tenant's 2025 account. It does not establish who is legally liable, that arrears block a name transfer, tenant authority to transfer the service, a billing error, or a BESCOM response.

claims.text: One prospective name-transfer user reported being unable to check progress because the one-time password was sent to the previous owner's phone number.
claims.notes: One 2026 report of a previous-contact dependency. It does not establish that an OTP is generally required, that it functions as legal consent, that the previous owner was unavailable, or the current correction path.

claims.text: One person who said their e-Khata had been completed reported that the BESCOM name-change login appeared to require a phone/OTP associated with the builder's contact and asked how to proceed without an offline route.
claims.notes: One 2026 account of a perceived login/contact obstacle. It does not prove the builder's contact was the only possible credential, a builder consent requirement, an e-Khata effect, or a current BESCOM rule.

claims.text: This bounded pass did not identify a sufficiently specific public first-person Bengaluru account of a BESCOM name-transfer attempt after the recorded consumer's death.
claims.notes: Searches were restricted to public first-person evidence. General guides, legal reporting, provider material, and non-Bengaluru accounts were excluded; this is not evidence that the route succeeds or fails.

roadblocks.title: Reported tenant reliance on an uncooperative owner for an account issue
roadblocks.symptom: One tenant reported pre-tenancy charges on the current bill and could not obtain cooperation from the property owner while concerned about an unpaid account balance.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Unknown; the account does not establish billing liability, account ownership, arrears status, a transfer request, or who could act for the service.
roadblocks.recovery: Obtain current written account and transfer guidance from BESCOM and retain tenancy/payment records; do not infer tenant authority or arrears liability from the citizen account.

roadblocks.title: Reported prior-contact credential obstacle
roadblocks.symptom: Two citizens reported that a name-transfer login or status check appeared to depend on a previous owner's or builder's recorded phone/OTP route.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Unknown; the accounts do not establish the authentication rule, record state, identity verification, consent status, or an available contact-update path.
roadblocks.recovery: Use BESCOM's current authorised support and account-correction route for the specific service; do not request, share, or use another person's OTP or treat it as consent.

roadblocks.title: No retained citizen account for a deceased-consumer transfer
roadblocks.symptom: Citizen evidence in this pass does not substantiate a lived BESCOM transfer route after the recorded consumer's death.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Unknown; absence of a usable public account is not evidence about the underlying procedure or its outcome.
roadblocks.recovery: Use current official and public-workflow sources for case-specific guidance; add a redacted public first-person account only if one is later found.
